title: WPSS/1907/2026 of DHARMENDER KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Single No. 1907 of 2026
20 July, 2026
Dharmender Kumar
--Petitioner
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand & others
--Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Vinay Kumar, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Manish Bisht, Brief Holder for the State-respondent nos.1 and 2.
Mr. Shailendra Noriyal, Advocate for respondent no.3.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
By means of the present writ petition,
petitioner is seeking a mandamus directing the
Selecting Body to revise the Provisional
Recommendation List dated 27.05.2026 and to
recommend the name of petitioner to the Appointing
Authority for appointment on the post of Instructor
(Electrical) against one of the unfilled vacancies
earmarked for candidates belonging to SC Category of
the advertisement dated 16th February, 2024.
2. The petitioner contends that the petitioner
participated in the selection process pursuant to the
advertisement dated 16.02.2024 Annexure-1 to the writ
petition for the post of Instructor (Electrical) in
Government ITI in the State of Uttarakhand.
3. The grievance of the petitioner as canvassed
in the present writ petition is that despite selection and
after appearing in the document verification process,
the name of petitioner was not recommended for
1

2026:UHC:6074
appointment to the appointing authority while name of
other candidates have been recommended.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that he had moved a representation to the respondent
no.3 on 29.06.2026 which is still pending disposal at
the end of the respondent/Commission.
5. It is contended by learned counsel for the
petitioner if a direction is issued to the
respondent/Commission i.e. the Selecting Body to
decide the representation of the petitioner within a
stipulated time fixed by this Court, the end of justice
would be met.
6. Learned counsel for the Commission does not
dispute if such a direction is issued to the Commission
to decide the representation submitted by the
petitioner.
7. Accordingly, writ petition is finally disposed
of directing respondent no.3 to decide the
representation of the petitioner dated 29.06.2026
(Annexure-10 to the writ petition) within a period of
four weeks from the date of production of certified copy
of this order strictly in accordance with law and after
giving opportunity of hearing to the petitioner.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
20th July, 2026
Ravi/Nahid
